questions.question: For what portion of the signal cycle does each active element in a push-pull, Class AB amplifier conduct?

choices.A: More than 180 degrees but less than 360 degrees

questions.answer: More than 180 degrees but less than 360 degrees

questions.question: What is a Class D amplifier?

choices.A: An amplifier that uses switching technology to achieve high efficiency
choices.B: A low power amplifier that uses a differential amplifier for improved linearity
choices.C: An amplifier that uses drift-mode FETs for high efficiency
choices.D: An amplifier biased to be relatively free from distortion

questions.answer: An amplifier that uses switching technology to achieve high efficiency

questions.question: What circuit is required at the output of an RF switching amplifier?

choices.A: A filter to remove harmonic content
choices.B: A high-pass filter to compensate for low gain at low frequencies
choices.C: A matched load resistor to prevent damage by switching transients
choices.D: A temperature compensating load resistor to improve linearity

questions.answer: A filter to remove harmonic content

questions.question: What is the operating point of a Class A common emitter amplifier?

choices.A: Approximately halfway between saturation and cutoff
choices.B: Approximately halfway between the emitter voltage and the base voltage
choices.C: At a point where the bias resistor equals the load resistor
choices.D: At a point where the load line intersects the zero bias current curve

questions.answer: Approximately halfway between saturation and cutoff

questions.question: What can be done to prevent unwanted oscillations in an RF power amplifier?

choices.A: Tune the stage for minimum loading
choices.B: Tune both the input and output for maximum power
choices.C: Install parasitic suppressors and/or neutralize the stage
choices.D: Use a phase inverter in the output filter

questions.answer: Install parasitic suppressors and/or neutralize the stage

questions.question: What is a characteristic of a grounded-grid amplifier?

choices.A: High power gain

questions.question: Which of the following is the likely result of using a Class C amplifier to amplify a single-sideband phone signal?

choices.A: Reduced intermodulation products

questions.question: Why are switching amplifiers more efficient than linear amplifiers?

choices.A: Switching amplifiers operate at higher voltages
choices.B: The switching device is at saturation or cutoff most of the time
choices.C: Linear amplifiers have high gain resulting in higher harmonic content

questions.answer: The switching device is at saturation or cutoff most of the time

questions.question: What is characteristic of an emitter follower (or common collector) amplifier?

choices.A: Low input impedance and phase inversion from input to output
choices.C: Acts as an OR circuit if one input is grounded

questions.question: In Figure E7-1, what is the purpose of R1 and R2?

choices.A: Load resistors

questions.question: In Figure E7-1, what is the purpose of R3?

choices.A: Fixed bias

questions.question: What type of amplifier circuit is shown in Figure E7-1?

choices.A: Common base

questions.question: What is the typical output impedance of an op-amp?

choices.A: Very low

questions.question: What is the frequency response of the circuit in E7-3 if a capacitor is added across the feedback resistor?

choices.A: High-pass filter

questions.question: What is the typical input impedance of an op-amp?

choices.A: 100 ohms

questions.question: What is meant by the term “op-amp input offset voltage”?

choices.A: The output voltage of the op-amp minus its input voltage
choices.B: The difference between the output voltage of the op-amp and the input voltage required in the immediately following stage
choices.C: The differential input voltage needed to bring the open loop output voltage to zero
choices.D: The potential between the amplifier input terminals of the op-amp in an open loop condition

questions.answer: The differential input voltage needed to bring the open loop output voltage to zero

questions.question: How can unwanted ringing and audio instability be prevented in an op-amp audio filter?

choices.A: Restrict both gain and Q

questions.question: What is the gain-bandwidth of an operational amplifier?

choices.A: The maximum frequency for a filter circuit using that type of amplifier
choices.B: The frequency at which the open-loop gain of the amplifier equals one
choices.C: The gain of the amplifier at a filter’s cutoff frequency
choices.D: The frequency at which the amplifier’s offset voltage is zero

questions.answer: The frequency at which the open-loop gain of the amplifier equals one

questions.question: What voltage gain can be expected from the circuit in Figure E7-3 when R1 is 10 ohms and RF is 470 ohms?
How does the gain of an ideal operational amplifier vary with frequency?

choices.A: It increases linearly with increasing frequency
choices.B: It decreases linearly with increasing frequency
choices.C: It decreases logarithmically with increasing frequency
choices.D: It does not vary with frequency

questions.answer: It does not vary with frequency

questions.question: What will be the output voltage of the circuit shown in Figure E7-3 if R1 is 1,000 ohms, RF is 10,000 ohms, and 0.23 volts DC is applied to the input?

choices.A: 0.23 volts

questions.question: What absolute voltage gain can be expected from the circuit in Figure E7-3 when R1 is 1,800 ohms and RF is 68 kilohms?
What absolute voltage gain can be expected from the circuit in Figure E7-3 when R1 is 3,300 ohms and RF is 47 kilohms?
What is an operational amplifier?

choices.A: A high-gain, direct-coupled differential amplifier with very high input impedance and very low output impedance
choices.B: A digital audio amplifier whose characteristics are determined by components external to the amplifier
choices.C: An amplifier used to increase the average output of frequency modulated amateur signals to the legal limit
choices.D: A RF amplifier used in the UHF and microwave regions

questions.answer: A high-gain, direct-coupled differential amplifier with very high input impedance and very low output impedance
